record.context_brief: Stein property of tangent bundles of Hessian manifolds
record.original_question: Let M be a Hessian manifold with Hessian metric g, and suppose that the Riemannian manifold (M, g) is complete. Is the tangent bundle of M, equipped with its natural complex structure, a Stein manifold? In particular, if Ω is a convex domain in ℝⁿ containing no complete straight lines and Γ is a discrete subgroup of the affine automorphism group of Ω acting freely and properly discontinuously on Ω, is the tangent bundle over the quotient Ω/Γ a Stein manifold?

evidence.quote: Let M be a Hessian manifold with Hessian metric g. Suppose that (M, g) is complete. Is the tangent bundle over M, equipped with a natural complex structure, a Stein manifold? A case of particular interest is when Ω is a convex domain in Rⁿ containing no complete straight lines, and Γ is a discrete subgroup of the affine automorphism group of Ω acting freely and properly discontinuously on Ω. Is the tangent bundle over the quotient space Ω/Γ a Stein manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A Hessian manifold is a triple $(M,\nabla,g)$ where $M$ is a smooth manifold, $\nabla$ is a flat torsion-free affine connection on $M$, and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$ that, in any $\nabla$-affine local coordinate system $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$, is locally given by $g_{ij}=\partial^2\varphi/\partial x^i\partial x^j$ for some smooth potential $\varphi$. The tangent bundle $TM$ carries a natural complex structure: in affine coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ on $M$ with fiber coordinates $(y^1,\dots,y^n)$, the functions $z^j=x^j+\sqrt{-1}\,y^j$ define holomorphic coordinates on $TM$, and with respect to this complex structure the Hessian metric $g$ on $M$ induces a Kähler metric on $TM$ with global Kähler potential. Recall that a complex manifold $X$ is called Stein if it is holomorphically convex and holomorphic functions on $X$ separate points (equivalently, $X$ admits a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion function).

Question. Suppose that $(M,\nabla,g)$ is a Hessian manifold for which the Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is complete. Is the tangent bundle $TM$, equipped with the natural complex structure described above, a Stein manifold?

Special case. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex domain that contains no complete affine line, and let $\Gamma$ be a discrete subgroup of the affine automorphism group $\mathrm{Aff}(\Omega)$ acting freely and properly discontinuously on $\Omega$, so that the quotient $M=\Omega/\Gamma$ inherits a Hessian structure. Is the tangent bundle $T(\Omega/\Gamma)$ a Stein manifold?
artifact.category_tag: Hessian manifolds and Stein tangent bundles
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface ongoing research on Hessian manifolds and Kähler/Born structures on their tangent bundles (e.g., recent 2025 preprints), but no source explicitly resolves whether the tangent bundle of a complete Hessian manifold (or of a quotient of a line-free convex domain by a properly discontinuous affine group) is necessarily Stein. The status of this specific question could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: On Topology and Geometry of Hessian Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses convexity theorems of Shima–Yagi and topology of complete/compact Hessian manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to develop the geometry of complete Hessian manifolds without explicitly settling Steinness of tangent bundles.

status_evidence.title: A Born Structure on the Tangent Bundle of a Hessian Manifold
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs Born/Kähler-type structures on TM induced by a Hessian metric on M.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the natural complex/Kähler structure on TM but does not resolve the Stein property in the complete case.
